query: What does secure attachment actually look like?
why_in_two_sentences: The #1 organic result (Britannica) is an encyclopedia entry and the #2 result (SimplyPsychology) is scoped to infants rather than the adult relationship question, so both were passed over and the top two on-query adult articles, AttachmentProject at #3 and ReachLink at #4, were judged instead. Our page out-covers AttachmentProject on every axis and matches ReachLink's identical concrete-behavior angle while going deeper on the loop mechanism, earned-versus-performed security, and the receiving problem, though ReachLink beats us on scannable structure and named research citations.
what_the_winner_does_that_we_dont: Add an in-page jump navigation / table of contents block near the top that links to each H2, the way ReachLink's 'In this Article' index lets readers skip to a section

Add a compact numbered 'things securely attached people do' catalog split by context (romantic / friendships / conflict / self-talk), like ReachLink's 25-item list, so the concrete behaviors are skimmable rather than buried in prose

Attach named-researcher provenance to the specific mechanism claims (e.g. Main & Hesse coherent-narrative / Adult Attachment Interview, Gottman flooding, Porges ventral-vagal state) rather than referring only to unnamed 'developmental research'
Add a short 'What secure attachment is NOT' bullet block that pre-empts the 'never jealous/never anxious' misconception up front, as ReachLink does in a labeled section

Include a side-by-side 'same trigger, three attachment responses' comparison covering more than one trigger (ReachLink runs five: silent partner, weekend-plans disagreement, criticism, partner needs space, forgotten reply)
what_we_do_that_they_dont: Break the pattern down into a named four-beat loop (signal, interpretation, protective behavior, relief) and pinpoint the interpretation step as the single intervention point
Distinguish earned, never-wounded, and performed security in a dedicated comparison table, which neither competitor does
Name the 'receiving problem' (affection discounted on the way in) as a separate machine from the forecasting/loss half
Provide a numbered practice protocol plus a one-week 'gap log' exercise the reader can start today
Ship a 34-question FAQ block with schema markup covering edge cases (single, cheating, aging, testing, relapse under load) far beyond the competitors' handful of FAQs
Include an explicit, high-placed 'when this belongs with a professional' safety boundary

above_the_fold.ours: A plain H1 restating the query, a boxed 'short answer' defining secure attachment as a run of small non-events, and an identify-box of verbatim intrusive-thought sentences; it earns the next scroll by naming the reader's exact experience rather than listing personality traits.
above_the_fold.theirs: ReachLink opens with a one-line summary, an 'In this Article' jump index, and a hook ('felt like something was missing?') plus the 'why it looks boring' reframe; the jump index earns the scroll by promising navigable depth immediately.
above_the_fold.gap: Add an in-page jump/table-of-contents index directly under the answer box so readers see the page's full scope and can navigate to their specific sub-question without scrolling blind.

questions_they_answer_that_we_dont: How do I know if I actually have a secure attachment style or if I'm just telling myself I do?
What does it actually feel like on the inside to have secure attachment compared to anxious or avoidant attachment?
Can working on your own attachment style actually change your relationships, or does the other person need to change too?
trust_signals: Ours carries a named founder author, first-person lived-experience specificity, and richer edge-case coverage, while ReachLink leans on named academic researchers and citations; ours wins on specificity and provenance but trails on formal citation.
one_change_with_most_traffic_impact: Add a scannable, context-grouped numbered catalog of concrete secure behaviors plus an in-page jump index near the top, capturing the skimmable-list and featured-snippet demand that ReachLink's '25 things' and jump nav are built to win.
